decisions.decision: How should classification work scale with demand?
decisions.context: The system processes millions of incoming documents per day, and volume varies strongly over the year. A queue can absorb bursts and let worker capacity scale with demand.

alternatives.label: Synchronous inference API
cons: Seasonal demand: callers face capacity spikes

alternatives.label: Queue-backed worker pool
cons: High volume: queue adds processing steps

alternatives.label: Scheduled bulk batches
cons: Seasonal demand: capacity changes less responsively

decisions.rationale: Seasonal demand decides the choice: a queue absorbs peaks while workers scale horizontally. This adds a queueing step and can increase time to results.
consequences: Workers need scaling and queue monitoring.
Result latency depends on backlog and capacity.

decisions.decision: How should classification results reach consuming teams?
decisions.context: Several teams consume classification results, so each needs a stable way to access them without coupling its workflow directly to the classifier.

alternatives.label: Direct integration from classifier to each team
cons: Multiple consumers: integrations multiply with each team

alternatives.label: Shared results API
cons: High volume: shared API must handle concurrent reads

alternatives.label: Shared results store with change events
pros: Multiple consumers: teams can consume independently
High volume: decouples reads from inference
cons: Multiple consumers: event and store operations add complexity

chosen.label: Shared results store with change events

decisions.rationale: Multiple consumers decide the choice: a shared store and events let teams integrate independently. Operating both components adds complexity.
consequences: Consumers need event handling and store access.
The store and event path need operational ownership.

decisions.decision: How should the system expose quality drift?
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. Input and output metrics can flag changes, while reviewed examples help check whether quality has actually changed.

alternatives.label: Aggregate input and output metrics
pros: High volume: inexpensive to compute at scale
cons: Quality drift: metrics are indirect quality signals

alternatives.label: Sampled case review
pros: Quality drift: operators inspect actual classifications
cons: High volume: samples cover only a fraction of cases

alternatives.label: Metrics with sampled case review
pros: Quality drift: combines broad signals with case inspection
cons: High volume: review requires sampling and operator effort

decisions.rationale: Operator visibility decides the choice: metrics can surface broad changes and sampled reviews provide case-level evidence. The trade-off is ongoing review effort, with samples unable to represent every case.
consequences: Provide operators with a review workflow.
Plan for review effort as volume changes.

decisions.decision: How should model changes be deployed and attributed?
decisions.context: The system needs to distinguish changes in classification behavior from changes in incoming documents. Recording the model version with each result supports comparisons when quality drift appears.

alternatives.label: Deploy the latest model without per-result versioning
cons: Quality drift: harder to attribute behavior changes

alternatives.label: Version models and record version per result
pros: Quality drift: compare results by model version
cons: High volume: store and manage version metadata

chosen.label: Version models and record version per result

decisions.rationale: Quality drift visibility decides the choice: per-result versioning supports attribution across model changes. It costs extra metadata storage and model lifecycle management.
consequences: Include model version in stored results.
Manage version lifecycle and rollback procedures.
